tests/tooling/verify/gates/section-facto.why: RETIRED WITH THE BEHAVIOUR IT PINNED (#1584). This file existed to pin two TOOL ERRORS that the legacy gate raised from its own type-alias resolver: a type-alias CYCLE threw, and an alias chain deeper than a fixed eight-hop budget threw. The #1584 conversion deletes that resolver — the final policy asks the checker for a parameter's resolved TYPE and compares its declaration to the one `packages/client/src/lib/registry.ts` exports as `ContributorRegistry`, which follows an alias chain of any depth with no recursion of its own and no budget to exceed. Both shapes are therefore no longer tool errors and ARE expressible as conformance rows, which is where they now live on the policy: the eleven-hop chain is a `mustFlag` (it is the same seam and it reds), and the circular alias pair is a `mustPass` (it resolves to no declaration, so it is simply not the registry, and a failed alias is not an accusation). Un-deletes if the policy ever re-acquires a gate-owned alias walk with its own cap or cycle detection — at which point those refusals become tool errors again and need a runPolicyPass pin, because a throwing example is a failed proof, never a proven refusal.

tests/tooling/warning-code-coverage.resi.why: RETIRED WITH ITS INJECTION SEAM (#1584). Every arm in this file was driven through `createWarningCodeCoverage([channel])`, an exported factory whose only purpose was to inject a channel carrying a NON-EMPTY `deferred` map, because the live channels both declared `deferred: {}` and the conformance runner can only drive the live descriptor. The #1584 conversion deletes both empty `deferred` tables (an empty exemption table whose stale/orphan arms are structurally unprovable is not a table) and the exported factory with them, so the two DEFERRED-ratchet arms have no subject left to test. The file's seven other arms were never blocked and are now proof rows on the final policy: the unrelated accumulator, the arbitrary matching literal, the aliased warnings sink, the quiet chat emitter, the returned warning payload, the tuple home excluded from its own emit corpus, and the #1440 mapper-rename tripwire. Un-deletes if a real deferral ever returns — but the destination law routes that to a warning `workItem` or an exact reviewed grant, neither of which needs a gate-owned map or an injected check.

tests/tooling/verify/gates/form-factory-.why: RE-POINTED, not dropped: this was the permanent #620 pin for `form-factory-for-multifield`, and it drove the LEGACY `gate.visitFile` through a hand-rolled `GateRunCtx`. That entry point ceased to exist when the module converted to `defineGate` (#1584) — a final policy has no `visitFile` the pin can call and no `scanRoot` it can assert — and the pin's token assertions (`"Probe (3 fields)"`) named a spelling the central `@orb-waive` grammar's position group `[^()\r\n]+` can never parse, so it was asserting the very defect the conversion fixed. Every one of its #620 cases — the 4-arm switch false positive, if/else, the ternary, `&&` guards, sibling conditionals, the fat arm, the mixed ternary, the nested render callback, the factory-import exemption — moved to `tests/tooling/verify/gates/ordinary-client-and-ct-wave.test.ts` and now runs through the PRODUCTION dispatcher (`runPolicyPass`), which is strictly stronger: it also asserts the reported position is paren-free authored text.
